answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a cedar-like stake: a refundable bond that matures slowly, like a tree, and is slashed when one operator spawns many fake agents. Trust should not peak at a single zenith score that bots can farm; instead, reputation accrues through repeated verifiable work across independent islands of demand, so a cheap clone cannot inherit history. Sybils stay expensive to plant and easy to prune.
